# RL78, checked against rl78-elf-as (GNU binutils). One statement per line.
#
# Addresses: 0xffe30 is a short-direct (saddr) address only, 0xfff20 an SFR
# only, and 0xfff10 lies in both ranges, which is where the per-instruction
# preference order shows.
#
# Not here, because rsasm differs from the reference on purpose or the
# harness cannot run them (tests/rl78.rs covers the first three, and the
# relocations of the last):
#   - the G14 multiply/divide group, which the reference rejects without -mg14;
#   - constants too wide for their field, which the reference truncates silently;
#   - relative branches within a few bytes of the short range, where the
#     reference's relaxation misjudges the reach;
#   - `.balign` as the last thing in .text, after which the reference also pads
#     the section's size;
#   - absolute references to labels in relocatable output, where the reference
#     also writes the address into the field it relocates.

# ---- no operands -----------------------------------------------------------
nop
brk
brk1
halt
stop
ret
reti
retb
ei
di
skc
skh
sknc
sknh
sknz
skz
mulu x
MULU X

# ---- symbolic operands -------------------------------------------------------
# The reference leaves these fields zero and emits a relocation.

bt a.1, $.+3
mov1 cy, sym.2
xch a, sym
movw bc, sym
